title: What does AMMDeposit do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of AMMDeposit and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, AMMDeposit contributes assets to an existing AMM and receives liquidity-provider tokens. [1]

The selected deposit mode determines whether one asset, both assets or a target LP-token amount controls the operation. Single-sided deposits can involve an implicit trade and different economics from proportional deposits. Check limits and resulting pool share. LP tokens represent exposure to pool assets, not an interest-bearing bank deposit or fixed redemption amount. [1]

The AMMDeposit reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using AMMDeposit, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
